findings.title: canManage() is granted by VIEW permission on all groups
findings.body: `canManage()` falls back to `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`. An admin who only holds the VIEW scope on the all-groups resource therefore passes `canManage()`. That check guards top-level group creation and moving groups (`GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` → `requireManage()`), and it is also reached through `canView(group)`-style checks in the parent class. This is a privilege escalation from view to manage. It should check only `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE`.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses resource ids and the wrong type lookup
findings.body:
In V2, per-group resources are created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource`. Their name is the group id and no type is set, so `findByType(server, "Groups")` only returns the all-groups resource named "Groups".

The callback then does `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)`, which looks the resource up by name using its id. That lookup always misses and falls back to the all-groups resource. It then adds `groupResource.getId()`, a resource id rather than a group id, to the result.

Consequences:
- Groups with individual VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions are never enumerated.
- When an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS permission exists, the returned set contains a non-group id. `UsersResource.searchForUser` and `getUsersCount` pass it as the `UserModel.GROUPS` filter, so searches and counts return zero users.

findings.title: Possible NPE when the all-groups resource is not resolved
findings.body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource` returns null when the schema is not supported, for example when `realm.isAdminPermissionsEnabled()` is false while the admin-permissions client still exists. The result is passed straight to `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and later dereferenced via `resource.getScopes()`. In that state any group permission check that falls back to all-groups throws a NullPointerException, which surfaces as a 500. The code should return false when `resource` is null.

findings.title: Group removal listener calls a V2 method that throws UnsupportedOperationException
findings.body: When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, the listener calls `management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false)` on GroupRemovedEvent. If ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is also enabled, `management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2`, whose new `GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` throws UnsupportedOperationException. Deleting any group then fails. Separately, V2 has no cleanup of per-group resources (named by group id) on group deletion, so orphaned resources remain.

findings.title: Wrong javadoc reference for requireManageMembers
findings.body: The javadoc for `requireManageMembers` says it throws if `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false. The implementation actually checks `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`, so the reference is wrong.

findings.title: canManage() javadoc documents VIEW as granting manage
findings.body: The javadoc for `canManage()` says that in V2, having VIEW or MANAGE on groups grants manage. This documents the incorrect behaviour described above. Only MANAGE should grant manage.
